To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the failure rates of devices are determined by the process parameter distributions; (2) the failure rates are not affected by the mean of the process parameter distributions, only the distributions are important; (3) the failure rates increase as the distributions become more non-Gaussian and as the distributions become wider; and (4) the failure rates can be predicted using the process parameter distributions.

(1) a failure rate prediction based on conventional life testing data is more accurate if the life test data is obtained from devices manufactured under the same process conditions as the devices for which the failure rate prediction is to be made; (2) the accuracy of failure rate prediction based upon conventional life testing can be improved by using the model developed in this paper.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for relating quality and reliability.
the development of a methodology to estimate the failure rates of semiconductor devices based on process parameter distributions.
a quantitative model that relates “process quality” to “reliability”.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method for predicting failure rates is a significant improvement over conventional methods.
the failure rate model is an excellent tool for predicting the reliability of semiconductor devices.
the failure rates for a given process can be estimated from a combination of the failure rates for each process step and the process yield.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show that it is possible to predict the reliability of semiconductor devices based on process quality.
we have developed a methodology that can be used to predict the reliability of a device based on process quality data.
the model can provide a more realistic failure prediction and a more accurate assessment of process capability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
failure rate predictions based solely on life test data are not realistic.
the quality of a semiconductor process is a major factor in the reliability of the devices produced.
a more realistic failure-rate prediction can be made by combining life-test data and process parameter distributions.
